title: Yash Unveils 'Toxic' Trailer at Bengaluru Event, Confirms Dual Father-Son Role
excerpt: The KGF star returns after a four-year hiatus with a gangster saga featuring Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, and an ensemble cast, releasing August 26 in IMAX worldwide.
body:
• Yash confirms dual role as father Raya and son Ticket in the gangster thriller directed by Geetu Mohandas, marking his return after four years since KGF: Chapter 2
  • Nayanthara plays Ganga, Yash's on-screen sister; Kiara Advani stars as Nadia and calls the film a career-defining moment
  • Budgeted at ₹500–1,000 crore, Toxic releases in IMAX worldwide on August 26 in Kannada, English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam
  • Shot over 200 days across five Indian cities with Hollywood action choreographer JJ Perry and cinematographer Rajeev Ravi

Trailer Drops at Star-Studded Bengaluru Event

https://youtube.com/watch?v=WVtuEwiylpY

Yash returned to the spotlight on Saturday with the trailer launch of Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups at a packed multiplex in Bengaluru. The KGF star, absent from screens for over four years, was joined by co-stars Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Tara Sutaria, Huma Qureshi, Rukmini Vasanth, director Geetu Mohandas, producer Venkat K. Narayana, and distributor Anil Thadani. Actor Shiva Rajkumar also attended.

The trailer confirmed what fan theories had long speculated: Yash plays a dual role as Raya and his son Ticket — also known as Rumi — placing a father-son conflict at the center of the film's gangster universe. The footage showcased explosive action sequences, striking period-era production design, and a web of rivalries among the ensemble cast.

Yash Confirms Nayanthara as His On-Screen Sister

In a revelation that upended expectations, Yash confirmed that Nayanthara plays Ganga, his character's sister — not a romantic interest as many had assumed. He praised her commitment to the role during his speech at the launch.

"It takes a lot of grace to choose this film and do what you have done. You are a lady superstar. You look badass — like the most badass sister anybody can have."

— Yash, at the Toxic trailer launch in Bengaluru

Yash also revealed that Tara Sutaria's role was expanded during production. "We increased your scenes more than what was written because of your fabulous presence, effort, and elegance," he told the actress.

Kiara Advani, who plays Nadia, described the project as transformative. "I truly believe that Geetu and Yash manifested for me to be Nadia in this film," she said. Nayanthara echoed the sentiment, telling Advani: "This is one of the best films you have done in your entire career. Toxic is going to be your best."

"I think there will be a Kiara before Toxic and Kiara after Toxic. You guys have spoiled me and every actor in this film. We are going to get so much greedier with every film that we step into."

— Kiara Advani

Four Years and 200 Days of Shooting

Toxic marks Yash's return to cinema after KGF: Chapter 2 (2022), which shattered box-office records across India. The actor co-wrote the screenplay with Geetu Mohandas, the acclaimed Malayalam filmmaker making her most ambitious project to date.

Principal photography stretched 200 days from August 2024 to October 2025, spanning Bengaluru, Mumbai, Goa, Thoothukudi, and Jaipur. The production deployed a crew of over 1,000 members and 450 actors, including international performers. Hollywood stunt choreographer JJ Perry designed action sequences alongside India's Anbariv duo, while cinematographer Rajeev Ravi and composer Ravi Basrur — reuniting with Yash for a third time after the KGF franchise — anchor the technical team.

The film's budget is reported between ₹500 crore and ₹1,000 crore, making it one of the most expensive Indian productions ever. Distribution deals have commanded massive figures: Lionsgate will handle the English-language release worldwide, while AA Films acquired North India and Nepal rights and Phars Film secured overseas distribution for ₹105 crore.

Global Release and Diaspora Reach

Toxic will release in standard and IMAX formats worldwide on August 26, coinciding with the Onam festival. Beyond its original Kannada and English versions, the film will be available in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam.

The cast includes Huma Qureshi as Elizabeth, Akshay Oberoi as Tony, Sudev Nair as Karmadi, and Rukmini Vasanth as Mellisa. Two singles — "Tabaahi" featuring Vishal Mishra and "Manamohaka" — have already built anticipation ahead of the trailer drop.

For the Indian diaspora, Toxic signals the continuing globalization of Indian cinema beyond Bollywood. Yash's KGF franchise helped establish Kannada cinema on the international stage, and the multi-language strategy with Lionsgate's global distribution points to even broader ambitions. With its massive scale and star-powered ensemble, the film is positioned as one of the biggest Indian releases of 2026.
